sentences.text: The juvenile holotype specimen of Chilesaurus is estimated to have been about 1.6 meters long in life.
Adult Chilesaurus is estimated to have reached a full length of about 3.2 meters.
Chilesaurus possesses unique skeletal features including a short premaxilla, a quadrilaterally-shaped coracoid, a hand with only two clawed fingers, and distinct hip and ankle structures.
Chilesaurus is distinguished by its unique spatula-shaped, elongated teeth that protrude forward from their sockets.
Chilesaurus measured approximately 3.2 meters from nose to tail.
Its small head featured small, spatulate teeth pointing obliquely forward, a unique trait among theropods.
An adaptation for eating plants included a pubic bone in the pelvis that pointed backward.
Its hind limbs were less adapted for running, indicated by a small cnemial crest on the front upper part of the tibia and a wide foot with a weight-bearing first toe.
It could defend itself with a robust arm equipped with two claws, the first being large and very extended, similar to basal sauropodomorphs.
If classified as a theropod, Chilesaurus would be one of very few non-coelurosaurian theropods to have evolved herbivory.
New specimens discovered in 2008 were initially thought to belong to several different dinosaur species, but were later found to belong to the same species with a strange combination of traits.
A seven-year-old boy named Diego Suárez discovered the first fossils of Chilesaurus on February 4, 2004.
The initial discovery of Chilesaurus occurred while its discoverer and his geologist parents were searching for decorative stones in Chile's Aysén Region.

The first fossils of Chilesaurus, a vertebra and a rib, were discovered on February 4, 2004, in Mallín Grande, Chile Chico commune, by seven-year-old Diego Suárez while accompanying his geologist parents.
The type species Chilesaurus diegosuarezi was named and described in 2015 by Argentine paleontologist Fernando Novas and his collaborators.
The holotype SNGM-1935 was found in a layer of the Toqui Formation dating to the late Tithonian.
The unique tooth structure of Chilesaurus indicates it was a herbivore, a trait rare among theropods.
Chilesaurus has a backward-pointing pubic bone, interpreted as an adaptation for a complex digestive system required for herbivory.
Researchers suggest Chilesaurus may have used its strong arms and large first finger claw for defense.
The classification of Chilesaurus is uncertain, with most researchers viewing it as a theropod and a minority suggesting it is an ornithischian.
Chilesaurus displays a mix of traits from theropods, ornithischians, and sauropodomorphs, challenging traditional dinosaur classification splits.
In 2017, Baron and Barrett proposed that Chilesaurus might be a basal member of the ornithischian group.
Despite subsequent studies, the classification of Chilesaurus remains uncertain as it has not been definitively tested as a theropod in all analyses.
Chilesaurus was originally placed in a basal position within the Tetanurae clade among theropods.
This genus shows a confusing mix of traits normally present in ceratosaurians, basal sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians.
Chilesaurus is classified under the parent group Ornithischia.
Chilesaurus lived approximately 148 to 147 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period in Chile.
Fossils of Chilesaurus were found at the Mallín Grande locality in the Chile Chico commune of the Aysén Region, Chile.
Chilesaurus coexisted with small theropods, basal crocodilians, diplodocid and titanosaurian sauropods, and possibly brachiosaurids in the Toqui Formation.
Chilesaurus lived during the Tithonian stage, from 149.2 to 143.1 million years ago.
It is debated whether Chilesaurus is a theropod or an ornithischian, though its theropod affinities are more widely supported by other researchers.

An alternative classification proposed by Baron and Barrett in 2017 suggests Chilesaurus could be a basal ornithischian, with ornithischians being closer to theropods than to sauropodomorphs, forming a group called Ornithoscelida.
